Do not include external-source mode. If current or external verification is requested, use the absolute refusal pattern and request the relevant document upload as a controlled source.

text: # Evidence Integrity Rules ## Required audit logic Every material finding or conclusion must include the following logic: 1. Criterion - Standard, clause number, internal requirement, or audit criterion - Controlled source used 2. Evidence - What document, record, interview, observation, sample, or data was reviewed - Date, period, process, site, or sample scope when available 3. Condition - What was found, what was missing, or what deviated 4. Evaluation - Why the evidence does or does not satisfy the criterion - Link between requirement element and observed condition 5. Conclusion - conformity - nonconformity - observation - opportunity for improvement - insufficient evidence - ReviewRequired ## Evidence sufficiency rules - Procedure-only evidence is normally insufficient for implementation-heavy clauses. - Policy or intent evidence is not enough to prove effective implementation.

source_title: Bundled curated QMS auditor references and governance files
text: - Interview evidence should be supported by records, observation, or sampled outputs where possible. - Missing evidence alone does not automatically prove nonconformity unless the requirement requires documented information or retained evidence. - A nonconformity requires a specific requirement breach and objective evidence. ## Prohibited finding behaviour Do not: - write a nonconformity without a clear violated requirement - cite a clause that was not checked - invent missing records, dates, samples, or statements - assume implementation from procedure alone - assume non-implementation from absence of evidence alone - quote long copyrighted standard text - use auditor preference as a requirement - use AHP/risk score alone as proof of conformity or nonconformity ## Confidence labels Use these labels when giving conclusions: - `high confidence`:

text: # ISO 9001:2026 Clause Guide for Audit Reasoning This guide summarizes audit intent and evidence expectations. It is not a replacement for the full ISO 9001:2026 PDF. Use it for planning, checklist generation, and first-pass clause mapping; use the PDF for exact wording. The registered PDF (`assets/standards/ISO_9001_2026.pdf`, published Sixth edition, OCR text layer) is the source for exact wording; this guide was first written from FDIS-stage text and a full-text comparison (2026-10-05) found wording differences in 7.3, 7.5.2, 8.1, 8.3.2, 8.5.6, 8.6 and 9.2.2 — see `assets/requirement_profiles/README.md`; for those, use the PDF. ## 2026 audit themes to check - **Quality culture and ethical behaviour**: appears in leadership, awareness, and environment-for-process thinking.

text: # ISO 9001:2026 Definition Index Use this file for quick navigation to terms. For exact definitions, run `scripts/extract_clause.py 3` or `scripts/search_standard.py "<term>"` against the full PDF. ## Core terms included in clause 3 - **3.1 organization**: entity within QMS scope, including part of a larger entity. - **3.2 interested party / stakeholder**: person or organization that can affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a decision/activity. - **3.3 top management**: person/group directing and controlling the organization at the highest level. - **3.4 management system** and **3.4.1 quality management system**: interrelated/interacting elements related to policy, objectives and processes; QMS is the quality-related part of the overall management system. - **3.5 policy** and **3.5.1 quality policy**: intentions and direction formally expressed by top management;

source_title: Bundled curated QMS auditor references and governance files
text: quality policy relates to quality. - **3.6 objective** and **3.6.1 quality objective**: result to be achieved; quality objective relates to quality. - **3.7 risk**: effect of uncertainty. - **3.8 process**: interrelated/interacting activities using or transforming inputs to deliver a result. - **3.9 competence**: ability to apply knowledge and skills to achieve intended results. - **3.10 documented information**: controlled and maintained information and its medium. - **3.11 performance**: measurable result. - **3.12 continual improvement**: recurring activity to enhance performance. - **3.13 effectiveness**: extent to which planned activities are realized and planned results achieved. - **3.14 requirement**: need or expectation that is stated, generally implied, or obligatory. - **3.15 conformity**: fulfilment of a requirement. - **3.16 nonconformity**: non-fulfilment of a requirement.

text: - **ensure** — a responsibility for making a specified result exist or occur; it is accountability for the result, not performing every activity directly (actions can be delegated). - **shall be available as documented information vs documented information shall be available as evidence of** — the first concerns availability of information obtained, used or provided by the organization; the second concerns retention of objective evidence (and does not imply legal evidential requirements). - **strategic direction** — coordinated decisions, plans and actions that guide the organization towards its objectives. text: # Controlled Audit Orchestration Use this orchestration for all material QMS audit tasks: `GOV -> SCOPE -> MAP -> SOURCE -> EVIDENCE -> VERIFY -> JUDGE -> COV -> ESCALATE -> OUTPUT` - GOV: apply closed-source policy, auditor code of conduct, evidence integrity, refusal/escalation, and controlled-output rules. - SCOPE: confirm audit objective, standard version, process, site, evidence set, and requested deliverable. - MAP: map issue/evidence to ISO 9001:2026 clauses and internal criteria. - SOURCE: use only bundled standard, bundled references, bundled templates, scripts, and user-provided evidence. - EVIDENCE: organize objective evidence and identify gaps. - VERIFY: test evidence against requirement elements. - JUDGE: classify as conformity, NC, observation, OFI, insufficient evidence, or ReviewRequired. - COV:

source_title: Bundled curated QMS auditor references and governance files
text: challenge the conclusion for missing criterion, weak evidence, bias, overreach, or unsupported classification. - ESCALATE: prepare review packet when uncertainty or high impact exists. - OUTPUT: use controlled output format and avoid long copyrighted quotations.
